order: Build the deterministic P0 substrate: recorded allowance readings in, the router's bucket-state shape out. Implement it with zero dependencies in CommonJS, mirroring the shape of the existing verifier and router substrates. Cover reading and throttle recording with hard input validation, a state function that produces exactly the router's expected input, the Amber-arm confirmation protocol, throttle prediction, reporting, and a CLI, plus a publish step. Do not fabricate denominators — derive state only from real readings, across vendors; ledger attribution stays out of scope and is registered as a follow-on. Record every design ruling — reserve source, staleness windows, confirmation semantics, throttle-prediction shape, the exhausted-evidence rule — in the module's own README, marking anything the plan leaves silent as an estimate or unstated. Prove interop against the router across green, below-reserve, unconfirmed-arm, hard-throttled, zero-reading, and exhausted cases. Gitignore the new runtime data files and wire the suite into CI after the router suite.
claims: We shipped a 914-line module and a 637-line test suite: 152 checks, all against temp-directory fixtures — the real project data files are never touched. Interop was proven against the live router: a green state dispatches end to end, a below-reserve reading fires the reserve gate, an unconfirmed arm fires and a recorded confirmation lifts it, a hard throttle takes the exhaustion recast, and an exhausted bucket forces mandatory review to not close. CI runs the suite right after the router's.
